$comment: Per-human deployment records driven by elohim/holochain/Jenkinsfile. All humans now run the consolidated single-container pattern (elohim-node) — see genesis/orchestrator/manifests/humans/_edgenode-consolidated.template.yaml for the shared template. Adam uses an explicit manifest file (the historical reference impl); everyone else sed-renders the template. See genesis/plans/2026-04-16-elohim-node-consolidation-design.md for background and 2026-04-21-consolidate-human-deployments.md for the migration that retired the legacy 4-container pattern. The edgenode{Memory,Cpu}{Request,Limit} fields are THE source of truth for per-human conductor resource budgets — each set is tied to a deviceArchetype from genesis/plans/2026-04-13-device-archetypes-design.md. Treat these as the archetype's validated minimum; when bumped temporarily to unblock work, leave an entry-level $comment noting the intended floor and the follow-up that restores it.

humans.name: adam
humans.affinityComment: Adam: remote-side bootstrap anchor on shem — mirrors Matthew's role across WireGuard
humans.$genesisPeerComment: Adam + Matthew form the genesis pair: each ingests content directly during seeding so the payload settles across two peers in parallel rather than serially through one. Currently masked by suspended:true (shem dead) — when adam returns, this flag re-activates the pair without a pipeline edit.
humans.$suspendedComment: shem decommissioned 2026-05-04 (PSU failure, physical death). 40 GiB openebs-hostpath PVC unrecoverable. Re-enable requires either replacement remote-labeled hardware OR re-bootstrap with new agent key (seeded chain lost). See COMPUTE-CAPACITY-REVIEW.md.

humans.name: matthew
humans.affinityComment: Matthew: household bootstrap anchor + doorway host — requires performance node
humans.$genesisPeerComment: Matthew + Adam form the genesis pair (see adam.$genesisPeerComment). With adam suspended, matthew is the sole genesis peer until shem is replaced; the pipeline tolerates 1..N genesis peers.
humans.$comment: TEMP BUMP (2026-04-17): seeder routes all /account/import traffic through matthew-alpha's storage; 4Gi/2000m OOMed with RESTARTS=2 serving 3409 content items to 33 parallel imports. Archetype floor for device-family-node-base is 1Gi/4Gi + 500m/2000m — restore once seeder import is split across peers or backpressure lands.

TEMPORARY BUMP (2026-05-05): jessica's edgenode OOM-flapping at 1536Mi limit (7 restarts in 26h, last OOMKilled 2026-05-05T18:43Z while serving content + handling app-WS authentication during a2o sweep). Cluster is also in scaled-down mode with shem decommissioned, so jessica picks up extra registration load via the hosted conductor pool (matthew/jessica/timothy is the only path for the 25 humans newly seeded by the iter-3 agencyPhase fix). Bumping 1536Mi → 3Gi to give ~2× headroom over observed RSS — same pattern as Timothy's 2026-04-21 chromebook bump (see Timothy's $comment block for the restoration chain). Restoration: when shem returns and the hosted-pool load drops back to baseline, restore to the device-recycled-laptop archetype floor at 512Mi/1536Mi.

humans.$comment: SECOND TEMPORARY BUMP (2026-04-21). History: Chromebook floor 384Mi/768Mi + 150m/500m → bumped 2026-04-17 to Jessica/Frank/Pete 'typical steward' tier (512Mi/1536Mi + 250m/1000m) to survive seed burst. That held for seeding but the 1536Mi limit OOMed during sustained content-serving: pod observed at ~1.5GB RSS while serving 3498-item inventory to 5 peers + handling Holochain app-WS authentication backlog (3 OOMKilled restarts within 19min, container-level exit 137). Bumped again to 1Gi/3Gi + 250m/1000m — doubles the limit, gives ~2× headroom over observed RSS. Restoration chain: to prove the device-chromebook-edu archetype we eventually tune all the way back to the floor below. Full design in genesis/plans/2026-04-13-device-archetypes-design.md.
